## Historical audit: S0237

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/audit_sources/raw_failures/scene_rsi_v2_2/r2/fixed_h/H0/fixed_version_test/commons_31294395/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines in this file; the supplied observations are complete line excerpts, not split observations.

**Goal versus interpretation:** The stated task was to reconstruct a 512 × 341 indoor photograph as separate 3D meshes, matching camera, framing, materials and occlusion (student `model_request`, line 1). The student's code interprets it as a Victorian bedroom; the reference image itself is not available for independent inspection here.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Student `model_response` line 3; `execute` line 4 | A full program specified multiple objects: room shell, windows, bed, chairs, screen, tables, rugs and pictures. It grouped bed and chair parts, rotated the chair and pillows, and specified procedural wallpaper, floor, camera and lighting. These are coded intentions, not proof of correct connections, pose or visual match. |
| `execution_result` line 5 | Step 1 failed before realization: coverlet fillet radius `.15` exceeded half its `.18` minimum dimension. No image was returned. |
| Student `model_request` line 6; `model_response` line 8; `execute` line 9 | The runner returned that traceback to the student. The revision reduced the coverlet radius to `.085` and the thin pillow edge radius from `.07` to `.045`. This is evidence of error-feedback use, not teacher guidance. |
| `execution_result` line 10 | Step 2 progressed to world setup but failed because `scene.world` was `None`; again, no image was returned. Thus neither camera/framing nor light, texture, occlusion or render quality was visibly validated. |
| Student `model_request` line 11; `model_response` line 13 | After receiving the second traceback and notice of zero executions remaining, the student returned another complete program. It creates and assigns a world if absent and introduces unique names for repeated scene and asset members. No execution of this revision is visible. |

**Outcome and autonomy.** Both recorded executions failed: an initial construction/API-constraint failure followed by a world-initialization failure. The final nonempty revision is untested; there is no visible successful build, render, `DONE`, or formal success result. This is a technical execution failure with an unknown final submission outcome, not evidence of geometric or visual algorithm failure. The student independently produced and revised code using runner feedback; session records report zero student tool calls (lines 2, 7, 12). No teacher input, diagnosis, proposed update, or adoption is recorded.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, validating primitive parameter bounds and initialization assumptions before consuming a limited render budget matters. Task-specific hypotheses—including whether the bed and chair parts actually connect, whether multiple objects survive naming collisions, and whether wallpaper, lighting and camera match the photograph—remain unresolved. Unique naming and world initialization in the final program are attempted remedies, not verified fixes; names and material labels alone establish neither appearance nor geometry.
